review.title: A CI step that hangs reports 'in progress' for six hours instead of failing
review.acceptance:
REQUIRED: the jobs in ci.yml and windows.yml get `timeout-minutes`, per step where a step has a credible hang and per job otherwise. THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. PL-0735 fixes the one step that hangs today; this makes the NEXT one visible. A step with no bound burns GitHub's six-hour default and reports 'in progress' the entire time -- indistinguishable, to the only readable channel this project has (annotations, because job logs need a login), from a runner that is merely queued. That is how CI #181 and #182 both sat unfinished without anyone treating it as a failure.

REQUIRED: each bound is derived from an OBSERVED duration and the derivation is written beside it. A number somebody felt was generous is a number somebody will raise the first time it fires. Observed today: e2e 5m 8s, e2e-typecheck 12s, and the Windows e2e-desktop job 3m 25s.

REQUIRED: the bound is not so tight that a slow runner reads as a defect. A timeout that fires on a cold cache teaches people to re-run rather than to read, which costs more than the hang.

OUT OF SCOPE: the control-plane performance work, which is PL-0735, and any change to what the steps do.
review.notes:
SPLIT OUT OF PL-0735 in round 112, carrying its clause verbatim. PL-0735 was filed holding ci.yml and `ai:claim` refused it on an overlap with PL-0728, which is in REVIEW for the rest of the round. Keeping both halves in one task meant neither landed; this one is BACKLOG until ci.yml frees.

Classification C (workflow/harness defect) under the round-112 directive's A-E scheme, same as PL-0735. P1 rather than P0 because PL-0735 removes the hang that exists; this prevents the one that does not exist yet.

review.title: A task parked for an external reviewer consumes local implementation capacity
review.acceptance:
claude-infra's maxParallel has gone 1 -> 2 (round 109) -> 3 (round 113) -> 4 -> 5 (round 114). Every raise was justified against the same three documented conditions and every one of them held. That is the symptom, not the cause.

THE CAUSE: usageByAgent counts REVIEW toward maxParallel, and REVIEW here usually means 'parked for gpt-architect', who is not a locally executable agent. So a lane whose entire output is awaiting an EXTERNAL verdict consumes its own implementation capacity, and the only lever available is a number that was never meant to be pulled five times.

REQUIRED: a task in REVIEW whose reviewAgent is not locally executable does not count toward its owner's maxParallel. It still holds its allowedPaths -- CONFLICT DETECTION MUST NOT CHANGE, and that is the whole safety argument for the capacity limit being loosenable at all: overlap is prevented structurally by allowedPaths regardless of owner or count.
REQUIRED: 'locally executable' is read from the registry, not hard-coded to gpt-architect.
REQUIRED: a task in REVIEW with a LOCAL reviewAgent still counts, because that reviewer is real work this organisation has to do.
REQUIRED: the capacity raises this defect forced are reconsidered once it lands. If the right number for claude-infra is 2, it should go back to 2.
REQUIRED: driven by a scenario over FIXTURES, not the live board, per this suite's own standing rule, and shown to fail before the change.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing activeStatuses, which conflict detection reads. Only the capacity computation moves.
review.notes: FILED ROUND 114 during the release sprint, at the moment a fifth raise became the alternative to leaving PL-0734 -- item 2 on the release-impact list, directly on the launch path -- unstarted. Filed rather than fixed on the spot because scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs is reserved by PL-0735 in review, and because a control-plane change made in a hurry during a release sprint is how a scheduler quietly starts producing different waves.

unit.evidence:
node scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs: 72 scenarios, all pass, 133.9s. repo:validate passed. ai:validate: 150 tasks, 9 agents, no errors.

SHOWN TO FAIL BEFORE THE CHANGE, as the acceptance requires and not merely asserted. With scenario 10u in place and scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs stashed back to its pre-change state, the suite stopped at:

  [ 148.6s] 10u. A lane parked for an EXTERNAL reviewer does not spend its own capacity
  AI control plane error: claude-lead is at maxParallel 2

That message IS the defect: claude-lead held two tasks in REVIEW for gpt-architect -- an agent this repository cannot run -- and could not claim a third with entirely disjoint paths. The implementation was then restored and the file compared byte-for-byte against the copy taken before stashing.

OVER FROZEN FIXTURES, never the live board, per this suite's standing rule. claude-lead's real maxParallel is 2 today and borrowing it would make the scenario a bet on that staying true.

FOUR CASES, and the three that are not the headline are the ones that keep this safe:
  1. two REVIEWs for gpt-architect (external) + one READY -> the claim now succeeds.
  2. two REVIEWs for claude-test (LOCAL) + one READY -> still refused at maxParallel 2. That review is work this organisation owes; the slot is honest.
  3. two REVIEWs naming "gpt-architekt", which is in no registry -> still refused. A typo in a field must not silently buy capacity, and this is the direction of error that is cheap to write and expensive to find.
  4. a REVIEW parked externally whose paths overlap a READY candidate -> STILL REFUSED, with "PL-CAP-0032 paths overlap active task PL-CAP-0031 owned by claude-lead".

Case 4 is the whole safety argument. conflictWithActive still reads active(), untouched, so a task in REVIEW keeps its allowedPaths reserved exactly as before; activeStatuses is unchanged. Overlap is prevented structurally by declared paths regardless of owner or count, which is precisely why capacity can be relaxed without two agents ever writing the same file. Re-proved against the LIVE board as well: PL-0738 and PL-0730 are both still refused on their real overlap with PL-0736.

LOCAL EXECUTABILITY IS READ FROM THE REGISTRY, not hard-coded: consumesCapacity asks agentExecutable(reviewer, d), the same question dispatch already asks, which resolves through the adapter serving that agent's kind.

TWO NUMBERS WHERE THERE WAS ONE, because they are now two facts. The status report would otherwise have shown capacity falling with no explanation of where the work went. It now reads, against the live board: "claude-infra: 0/5 capacity in use, 3 active (3 parked for an external reviewer)" -- which is the five-raise situation, stated.

FOUND WHILE DOING THIS, recorded as its own defect.found: the suite's summary line carried a hand-typed "(73 scenarios)" and was wrong by two -- 71 call sites existed, 72 now. A false number inside a PASSING suite's own report. The count is derived in scenario() now and cannot drift.

NOT DONE, AND SPLIT OUT AS PL-0747: the acceptance's final clause, reconsidering the raises. control/agents.json is in this task's reviewDependencies and not its allowedPaths, so this task cannot write it -- and the clause itself says "once it lands", which has not happened. Judging whether 2 is right for claude-infra needs the board observed under the new accounting, and lowering numbers in the same commit that changes how they are counted would put two decisions under one review.

review.title: The commander's qualification evidence is collected by hand, one command at a time
review.acceptance:
PW-0504 is the OBSERVATION and stays blocked on hardware. This is the PREPARATION, which is engineering, and gpt-architect's round-115 section 4 asks for it by name: 'First prepare the smallest deterministic qualification package/checklist... Prepare this so Diego's part is minimal.'

TODAY THE RUN SHEET ASKS THE COMMANDER TO TYPE POWERSHELL AND PASTE OUTPUT. Step 0 alone is three separate snippets plus two settings pages read by eye, and every later row asks him to notice and copy something. Each hand-copied field is a field that can be wrong, missing, or from the wrong machine, and 'a RIG pass on unrecorded hardware is not evidence' is this document's own rule.

REQUIRED: one command Diego runs AFTER installing and launching, which collects everything collectable without him transcribing anything -- the environment block the matrix specifies (Windows build, GPU and driver, WebView2 runtime, display, audio), the installed tree's location and whether verify-install accepts it, whether sidecar.log exists with its size and tail, whether a liberty-desktop.exe process and its node.exe child are running, and whether the handshake line is present in the log.
REQUIRED: it writes ONE file he sends back, and prints a short human summary so he can see whether it worked before sending it.
REQUIRED: ABSENCE IS RECORDED, NOT SKIPPED. A missing sidecar.log, an unresolvable WebView2 version or a process that is not running are findings the report must state explicitly -- the run sheet already says an absent log is itself a finding, and a collector that silently omitted it would undo that.
REQUIRED: IT CLAIMS NOTHING IT CANNOT SEE. It must not report that WebView2 rendered the application, that playback worked, or that the window appeared. Those are the commander's eyes and the report must say so where it would otherwise be read as covering them. gpt's round-105 section 9: do not collapse those claims.
REQUIRED: NO SECRETS. It must not capture the launch token, environment dumps, or anything from the handshake line beyond host and port.
REQUIRED: testable off Windows. Every platform fact arrives through an injected reader, the way installed-identity.mjs takes `env` as a parameter, so the composition and the absence-handling have a suite on this machine. The Windows commands themselves cannot be executed here and that limit is stated rather than glossed.
REQUIRED: the run sheet's Step 0 and its report format point at the command instead of listing snippets to retype, and the rows only a person can judge stay a person's.

OUT OF SCOPE: marking any PW-0504 row passed. This task delivers the collector; the evidence is still the commander's to produce.
review.notes:
FILED ROUND 115 under gpt-architect's instruction to minimise the commander's work before asking for it. The one-command shape is chosen because the alternative already exists and is the problem: the run sheet is correct and it is long, and length is what makes a qualification session get abbreviated.

Scope held deliberately narrow. This does not automate judgement -- G1's compositing result, G2's scaling, the SmartScreen wording, whether a window actually appeared -- only the facts a machine can read about itself.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs: 18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail. node --check clean. repo:validate passed. node --test scripts/assert-no-row-runs-nowhere.test.mjs: 14/14, unaffected.

THE FIX, AND IT IS NOT A REDACTOR. gpt-architect's finding was correct: sidecarLog returned tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES), which put whatever happened to be in the log -- a token in a URL, an argv, an environment dump -- into a file written to be pasted into a chat. The tail is GONE. In its place, classifyLog() reads the same 16 KiB window and reports ONLY which entries of a fixed signature table matched, plus line and byte counts.

AN ALLOWLIST, NOT A DENYLIST, and that choice is the substance of the fix. Redacting things that "look like secrets" cannot work, because a secret is whatever happened to be in that file and no pattern enumerates it. So nothing the log said can reach the report: the report can only say which of ten patterns written in this repository matched, which is a fact about the table rather than about the file. Each pattern carries a plain-English `means` written here for a reader who has the report and not the machine -- which is the diagnostic value the raw tail had, minus the bytes. The ten: port-in-use, address-unavailable, permission-denied, file-missing, module-missing, module-format, native-module-failed, node-not-found, unhandled-error, fatal.

THE DANGEROUS FAILURE MODE OF AN ALLOWLIST IS HANDLED AND TESTED. A real error nobody wrote a signature for returns an empty list, which reads like "no problem". The note distinguishes them in those words -- "NO RECOGNISED FAILURE SIGNATURE in the examined window. That is not the same as 'no error'" -- it names the file to edit, and it points at the log on the machine, so nothing diagnostic is lost; it just does not travel unless the commander chooses to send it.

THE TEST THE REVIEWER ASKED FOR, AND WHY TWO TESTS THAT EACH LOOKED RIGHT LEFT THE LEAK UNCOVERED. There were already two: one asserted the fixture secret was absent from JSON.stringify(log.handshake) -- one subtree of the returned object -- and one asserted the WHOLE report was clean but fed sidecarLog a CLEAN log fixture. Between them, neither could ever have seen the tail. Now: the fixture hides the same string in THREE places, including an argv line and a URL inside an error line that the handshake logic never looks at; the sidecarLog test asserts on JSON.stringify(log) entire; and the existing full-report test was STRENGTHENED to use that adversarial fixture rather than a second near-duplicate test being added beside it. Both also assert that no raw log line, no URL from the log and no "[out]" prefix reaches the report, and the human-readable summarise() output is checked too, because that is what actually gets pasted.

SIX MUTANTS, ALL CAUGHT: (1) restoring tail: text.slice(-LOG_TAIL_BYTES); (2) adding a "harmless" lastLine field; (3) having the classifier quote the line it matched; (4) deleting the module-format signature from the table; (5) softening the no-signature note to "Nothing to report."; (6) making the examined window unbounded. All six reverted, 18/18 green afterwards. Mutant 4 is caught by a new test that drives one sample line through every pattern in the table, because a table nobody checks grows a dead entry.

docs/WINDOWS_CERTIFICATION.md no longer tells the commander the report carries the log's tail, states that it never quotes sidecar.log, and says why an allowlist rather than a redactor.

A SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST, REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED, AND IT IS ARGUABLY THE WORSE OF THE TWO: scripts/windows/qualify.test.mjs RUNS NOWHERE. It is not in package.json's test:scripts, and no workflow invokes it -- grep across package.json and .github/workflows finds only test-lifecycle.mjs under scripts/windows. So this task's `unit` gate is a suite that executes only when someone types the command by hand, and the leak was caught by a human reading the code rather than by the suite, which would not have run in any case. I have NOT fixed it: package.json and the workflows are outside this task's allowedPaths, and widening a reviewed surface mid-cycle is the thing the path lock exists to prevent. PL-0730 -- "test:scripts and the CI validate job can disagree in one direction without anything noticing" -- is where it belongs, and it is currently deferred behind PL-0736. Flagging it in the handoff.

STATED, NOT GLOSSED, and unchanged from round 1: none of the PowerShell in qualify.mjs has been executed. Every reading is a Windows fact and this container is Linux. What is proven here is the composition, the absence-handling, the bounding and now the sanitisation, all through injected readers.

review.title: A pasted addon manifest URL has no safe path into the adapter
review.acceptance:
FILED UNDER gpt-architect's ROUND-115 SECTION 6, WHICH BEGINS BY FORBIDDING THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION: "A repository audit found that Liberty ALREADY contains a substantial Stremio stream adapter under packages/provider-sdk/src/stremio/. DO NOT BUILD ANOTHER STREMIO CLIENT." This is a thin path ONTO that adapter and adds no protocol code, no second transport and no second rights model.

WHAT IS MISSING TODAY. Every piece of the flow exists except the first step and the shape that carries it. `checkUrl` validates, `fetchJson` resolves-and-pins and fetches, `parseStremioManifest` parses, `defineStremioSource` gates rights. Nothing accepts a `stremio://` URL -- the scheme has zero occurrences in the repository -- and nothing produces an object a UI can show a human BEFORE a source exists.

REQUIRED: `stremio://` is normalised to `https://` BEFORE the URL and network policy run, never after. A policy that runs on a scheme it does not recognise rejects a legitimate paste; a policy that runs after an unvalidated rewrite is a policy that judged a different URL than the one fetched. The normalisation is a scheme swap and nothing else -- it must not rewrite a host, a port or a path, and `stremio://` pointing at a loopback or private host is subject to exactly the same refusals as `https://` pointing there.

REQUIRED: the fetch goes through the EXISTING pinned transport in http.ts. Add-by-URL is precisely the transition url-policy.ts names -- "the moment this becomes the general server-side client for arbitrary operator- or user-configured addons, host-string checks are no longer a control at all" -- and the reason this task is safe to write is that PL-0710 already landed resolve-and-pin. No code path here may reach the network any other way.

REQUIRED: the result is a PREVIEW, and the type must make it impossible to mistake for an authorization. Name, version and declared resources, taken from the parsed manifest. It carries no `ContentRights`, is not branded `RIGHTS_DECLARED`, and cannot be handed to `createStremioProvider`. Section 7 of the directive is the invariant: "Stremio protocol compatibility is NOT playback authorization. A pasted URL must NEVER automatically become an authorized production source."

REQUIRED: becoming a source remains `defineStremioSource`, unchanged, with an explicit operator `rights` and `rightsBasis`. The preview feeds the form; it does not substitute for it, and nothing in it may be defaulted into a rights basis.

REQUIRED: every refusal is a typed reason, never a throw, matching the convention the rest of this directory already holds.

OUT OF SCOPE, and deliberately so: the settings UI, any API route, any persistence of user-added sources, and profile/repository scoping for them. Those are PL-0744 and they carry questions this task must not answer by accident -- whose rights declaration a user-added source carries, and whether a non-operator may add one at all.
review.notes: SPLIT FROM THE DIRECTIVE'S PRIORITY 5 ON PURPOSE. The directive describes the whole flow ADD-ONS -> ADD BY URL -> paste -> validate -> preview -> rights declaration -> save/enable. The SDK half is thin, reuses the existing adapter entirely and is the piece every possible UI shape needs. The UI half is a settings surface, an API route, a schema change and a rights-ownership question, which is not thin, is not release-critical for the primary journey, and would pull a security and rights review into a release sprint in order to ship a feature nobody has asked to use yet.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck in packages/provider-sdk (tsc --noEmit): clean. Caught a real defect first -- one normalizeAddonUrl call site still passed a single argument after the signature took the UrlPolicyOptions, TS2554 at add-by-url.test.ts:118. Repository-wide npm run lint: 12/12 tasks successful, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unused-import warnings in apps/web, untouched by this task).

unit.evidence:
npx vitest run in packages/provider-sdk: 13 files, 310 tests, all pass. add-by-url.test.ts contributes 22, and they were MUTATION-TESTED rather than merely observed green:

(1) MUTANT 'the convenience hole' -- make a stremio:// paste skip checkUrl (if (!checked.ok && !normalizedFromStremioScheme)). FIVE tests fail, including every identity case that runs the same host through both spellings and requires the outcomes to match. This is the defect the feature could most plausibly have shipped with.
(2) MUTANT 'unanchored regex' -- /stremio:\/\//i instead of /^stremio:\/\//i, so a stremio:// inside a query parameter gets rewritten. 1 test fails.
(3) MUTANT 'weakened note' -- replace the authorizationNote text with 'ok to use'. 1 test fails.

Under mutant (1) the rebinding case still PASSED, correctly: that defence lives in http.ts and the mutant did not touch it. The layering is asserted, not assumed.

NOT CLAIMED: no test here opens a real socket. resolve-and-pin.test.ts and pinned-transport.test.ts own that, and this file reuses their rig shape so that only the resolver and the transport port are doubles -- every refusal observed is produced by the production checkUrl / authoriseResolvedTarget path.

review.title: Every msiexec call in the lifecycle harness can wait forever
review.acceptance:
FOUND BY PL-0736 WHILE BOUNDING THE STEP THAT CONTAINS IT. `lifecycle.mjs` calls `spawnSync("msiexec.exe", args, { encoding: "utf8", windowsHide: true })` four times -- install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall -- and passes no `timeout`. Windows Installer serialises on the `_MSIExecute` mutex and a holder makes the next invocation WAIT rather than fail, so there is no deadline anywhere in the chain that decides F1, F3 and F4.

PL-0736 put a 15-minute `timeout-minutes` on the step. That is an OUTER bound and deliberately not the fix: when it fires, the whole step dies and the report says nothing about which case stalled or why.

REQUIRED: a `timeout` on each msiexec invocation, and a timed-out case REPORTED as a case outcome with its own reason, not collapsed into a crash. The harness already distinguishes exit 1 (a real case failure) from exit 2 (a refusal over arguments or platform) precisely so a configuration mistake is not filed as a product defect; a stall is a third thing and must not be filed as either.

REQUIRED: the bound is per-invocation and derived. A silent install of this MSI is seconds of work.

REQUIRED: a timed-out case is NEVER recorded as pass, and never as not-run with a reason that reads like a deliberate skip -- F2's `not-run` means 'the evidence does not exist', and a stall means 'we did not find out'.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what any case does, and the step-level bound PL-0736 added, which stays as the outer limit.
review.notes: P2 rather than P1 because the outer bound now exists, so the failure mode is 'the step dies at 15 minutes with a poor message' rather than 'the job burns an hour'. It is still a real defect: the message is what a person reads at 2am.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs: 42 tests, 42 pass (was 33; this task adds 9). Full npm run test:scripts: green, rc=0. repo:validate: passed.

TWO CASES RUN A REAL CHILD RATHER THAN ASSERTING A BELIEF ABOUT spawnSync. The whole repair rests on Node's timeout semantics, so they are exercised: a child that sleeps 60s with timeout 250 returns status null and error.code ETIMEDOUT; a missing binary returns status null and error.code ENOENT. THAT PAIR IS THE DEFECT -- the old code tested status !== 0, so a stall and an absent msiexec.exe both arrived as a bare fail with status: null and nothing to read.

MUTATION-TESTED, five ways this repair could be undone:
  no-timeout        (delete timeout from the spawn options)   -> 1 test fails
  stall-is-notrun   (a stall recorded as not-run)             -> 2 tests fail
  gate-off          (jobFailed returns false)                 -> 2 tests fail
  spawn-as-stall    (a spawn failure dressed as a timeout)    -> 1 test fails
  timeout-too-long  (180s -> 300s)                            -> 1 test fails

The first and last are the ones worth naming. no-timeout is the mutant every other case in this block would survive, because they drive classifyInvocation with synthetic results and would keep passing while timedOut quietly never became true again on a machine nobody in this container can run; it is caught only because the spawn options are a frozen exported value with an assertion on them. timeout-too-long is caught because the step bound arithmetic is ASSERTED rather than left in a comment: four invocations at 300s is 20 minutes against PL-0736's 15-minute timeout-minutes, so the step would die with no report and the deadline would have bought nothing.

NOT CLAIMED: nothing here runs msiexec, and no Windows machine was involved. What is tested is the decision -- what an invocation means -- which is the same division the rest of this harness keeps between residue.mjs deciding and msiexec measuring.

review.title: Experiment 1a FAILED on real hardware and D1 still reads as if it had not been tested
review.acceptance:
THE RESULT, FROM THREE REAL-HARDWARE RUNS ON THE COMMANDER'S MACHINE. Run 1 (PL-0748's instrumentation) proved the harness could not explain itself. Run 2 (PL-0749's geometry fix) proved the child HWND was being resized to nothing. Run 3 (PL-0750's WebView2 transparency fallback) proved the remaining question: mpv initialises, the HEVC file opens, D3D11 comes up on an RTX 3050, d3d11va hardware decoding is active, the VO is gpu-next at 1280x720, the first video frame is reported shown, the Pause button reaches mpv, AND put_DefaultBackgroundColor(0,0,0,0) is accepted and reported successful. The commander still sees NO VIDEO -- only the WebView UI.

THE VERDICT, SCOPED TO EXACTLY WHAT WAS TESTED. The arrangement in section 1 -- a sibling child HWND at HWND_BOTTOM beneath a WINDOWED WebView2 controller, made transparent through put_DefaultBackgroundColor -- FAILS visible composition. Criterion 1 (hardware decode) PASS. Criterion 3 (click and control) PASS. Criterion 2 (compositing) FAIL. Criteria 4 through 7 UNOBSERVED, because they are behind criterion 2. Overall Experiment 1a NOT PASS.

REQUIRED: SECTION 1 STOPS READING AS IF THE ARRANGEMENT WERE PROVEN. It currently says 'This is not a theory' and cites Stremio shipping it. That citation is still true and must not be deleted -- what must be added is that OUR implementation of the same arrangement was tested on real hardware and did not composite, and that the difference between Stremio's result and ours is not yet explained. An unexplained difference from a shipping product is a finding, not a footnote.

REQUIRED: THE FAILURE IS RECORDED WITHOUT OVERSTATING ANYTHING ELSE. The run does not prove WebView2 cannot composite, does not prove Tauri is the wrong shell, does not prove DirectComposition will work, and does not prove Stremio's shipping arrangement is broken. It proves that THIS arrangement, as this harness built it, did not show video on one machine. Every sentence recorded must be defensible at that width.

REQUIRED: SECTION 10'S PASS CRITERIA ARE MARKED WITH WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, per criterion, rather than left as empty checkboxes that imply the experiment was never run. The matrix stays UNMET: one machine is not the matrix, and nothing here may be read as covering Windows 10 22H2, an Intel or AMD iGPU, a hybrid-graphics laptop, or a DPI transition.

REQUIRED: SECTION 11 (VERIFICATION STATUS) CARRIES THE RESULT. That section exists because the reviewer's standing complaint is documents claiming more than their evidence. review.title: The installed MSI never starts its sidecar, and the splash spins forever instead of saying so
review.acceptance:
THE SYMPTOM, FROM THE COMMANDER'S INSTALLED MSI: the window shows "PROJECT LIBERTY -- Starting... -- Preparing the local service" indefinitely. His captured log shows bundled node.exe being launched and then dying with: Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, lstat 'C:', at Object.realpathSync, at Function._findPath, at resolveMainPath. So node starts and cannot resolve the main script it was given.

WHAT IS PROVEN FROM CODE, AND WHAT IS NOT. Proven: Node's resolveMainPath calls Module._findPath, which for the main module calls toRealPath -> fs.realpathSync on the resolved request; realpathSync splits the root with the regex /^(?:[a-zA-Z]:|[\\/]{2}[^\\/]+[\\/][^\\/]+)?[\\/]*/ (read out of the installed node binary, not from memory) and lstats that root on Windows. Proven: plan_launch builds both paths with Path::join against constants that contain FORWARD SLASHES -- "sidecar/node.exe" and "sidecar/server/liberty-sidecar.js" -- so the joined path has mixed separators. NOT proven: which of those produced the literal string 'C:' in the error. The pasted log shows backslashes where the constants have forward slashes, so separator detail has been normalised out of the transcript and the exact bytes Node received are not recoverable from it. An attempt to read the real log file was made and the folder-access request went unanswered.

REQUIRED: THE PATHS HANDED TO NODE ARE PLAIN AND PLATFORM-SEPARATED. Two independent defects are fixed rather than one guessed at, because each is wrong on its own terms. (a) A relative path written with forward slashes must be joined COMPONENT BY COMPONENT so the platform separator is used; under a Windows extended-length prefix the OS does not translate a forward slash at all, which Microsoft documents, so a mixed-separator path is not merely untidy. (b) Any \\?\ extended-length prefix must be removed before the path reaches Node, because Node's own module resolver reasons about Windows roots with the regex above rather than through the Win32 path parser.

REQUIRED: THE UNC FORM IS LEFT ALONE. \\?\UNC\server\share is NOT stripped: the correct plain form is \\server\share and a naive prefix removal would produce a path that silently addresses something else. Only the drive-letter form \\?\X: is normalised, and the UNC case is tested.

REQUIRED: THE COST OF STRIPPING IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The extended-length prefix exists to escape MAX_PATH. Removing it reintroduces that limit for these paths. That is accepted because Node cannot consume the prefixed form at all, so the alternative is not a longer path but no launch; and the MSI's own install location is far under the limit. It is recorded in the source so a future reader does not rediscover it as a surprise.

REQUIRED: THE LAUNCH LOG RECORDS THE ARGUMENTS, NOT JUST THE EXECUTABLE. The host currently logs only launch.node, which is why this round could not establish what Node actually received. It must log the full argument vector and the resolved paths. The token is provably not among the arguments -- launch_arguments returns one element and the_token_never_reaches_the_spawn_arguments asserts it -- and that property must be re-asserted now that the argv is written to a file a person will paste.

REQUIRED: A STARTUP FAILURE IS VISIBLE WITHOUT DEPENDING ON A LISTENER THAT MAY NOT EXIST YET. apps/desktop/dist/index.html registers its handler with `await listen("liberty://startup-failure", ...)`. That await resolves asynchronously, and a sidecar that dies in milliseconds reaches surface_failure before it does. Tauri does not replay events, so the failure is emitted into nothing and the splash spins forever -- which is exactly what the commander saw, and it means the supervision machinery worked and the report was lost. The failure must reach the page whether or not a listener is registered at the moment it happens.

REQUIRED: THE REGRESSION TEST SPAWNS A REAL NODE. A mocked ShellHost cannot catch this class of defect: every existing ordering test passed while the installed application could not start. The test must run the actual node executable against a script at an installed-style path CONTAINING SPACES, and assert it executes. On Windows it must additionally construct the extended-length form and demonstrate the difference between the raw and normalised paths, so the fix is pinned to observed behaviour rather than to a reading of documentation.

MUST NOT: weaken sidecar authentication, the loopback bind, the handshake's host refusal, origin or Host-header validation, the request guard, or the token's absence from argv. None of those is implicated and none may be touched to make a path problem go away.

MUST NOT: leak the token into the log, into the argv, into a path, or into any user-visible failure text. The log gains the argument vector this round, which makes that property load-bearing rather than incidental.

MUST NOT: claim the installed application works. CI can establish that node resolves a script at a spaced installed-style path and that the shell's ordering and failure handling hold. It cannot establish that the MSI starts, that the handshake completes on a real machine, or that the UI renders. That is the commander's MSI test and it is the only thing that can close this.

review.title: The installed application answers Internal Server Error: the packaged tree points at the build machine
review.acceptance:
THE SYMPTOM, FROM THE COMMANDER'S INSTALLED MSI AT f60f2fa. The bundled node.exe launches, the handshake completes -- liberty-sidecar-ready {"host":"127.0.0.1","port":65150} -- and the application then displays Internal Server Error. The captured stderr: Error: Failed to load external module pg-587764f78a6c7a9c / Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND] / Imported from: C:\\Program Files\\Project Liberty\\sidecar\\server\\dist\\desktop\\server\\chunks\\ssr\\[turbopack]_runtime.js. So rounds 127-129 all worked: the sidecar starts, the handshake lands, and the webview is reaching the server. What fails is one module resolution inside it.

THE ROOT CAUSE, ESTABLISHED FROM THE BUILD OUTPUT AND REPRODUCED LOCALLY, AND IT IS NOT A MISSING DEPENDENCY. Next 16.3.1 builds the desktop target with Turbopack. Turbopack externalises some server packages and emits a BARE import of a hashed alias for each: the shipped chunk [root-of-the-server]__0vd44rx._.js contains await a.y("pg-587764f78a6c7a9c"), and [turbopack]_runtime.js's externalImport does await import(id) with that string. Next materialises the alias as a RELATIVE SYMLINK in the build output: dist/desktop/node_modules/pg-587764f78a6c7a9c -> ../../../../../node_modules/pg, which inside the standalone tree resolves to standalone/node_modules/pg. package-sidecar.mjs then copied that tree with fs.cpSync, whose behaviour for a symlink is to resolve the link against its SOURCE directory and write an ABSOLUTE link at the destination (demonstrated in isolation on node v22.22.2: a relative link ../../target became an absolute path into the source tree). The packaged tree therefore shipped server/dist/desktop/node_modules/pg-587764f78a6c7a9c pointing at a directory on the GitHub runner. On the installed machine that path does not exist.

COPYING pg IS NOT THE FIX, AND THE COMMANDER WAS RIGHT TO SAY SO. pg and all nine of its transitive dependencies are already traced into standalone/node_modules by Next's file tracing and already copied to sidecar/server/node_modules/pg by this script. Nothing is missing from the installer. A POINTER leaves the tree. Adding a second copy of pg would have made the symptom disappear while leaving every future externalised package -- and every other symlink any build ever emits -- to fail the same way.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, which is what the remedy has to answer. sidecar-bootstrap/acceptance.mjs already starts the packaged sidecar and already asserts GET / -> 200. It passes, because on the build machine that absolute link RESOLVES. A tree that is only wrong RELATIVE TO BEING MOVED cannot be caught by any check that does not move it, and no check in this repository moves it. That is the class, and it is wider than this bug: it is every way a packaged artifact can depend on the machine that produced it.

REQUIRED: NOTHING IN THE PACKAGED TREE RESOLVES OUTSIDE IT. The external aliases are materialised into real directories of real files -- what an installer can carry -- rather than repaired as links, because a repaired link still has to survive WiX, an MSI, and whatever a future Windows does about symlinks, and a real file survives all three by not being a question. Materialisation runs to a FIXED POINT with a stated pass budget, because materialising one link can introduce others.

REQUIRED: THE FLAG IS NOT TRUSTED, THE RESULT IS ASSERTED. cpSync's dereference: true option selects the stat applied to the copy ROOT; a symlink NESTED in the tree is still copied as a link. Measured, not assumed: with dereference: true the destination's lstat().isSymbolicLink() is still true on node v22.22.2. Packaging therefore ends with an independent walk of the produced tree that refuses any symlink which does not resolve inside it, dangling ones included.

THE SYMPTOM, FROM THE OPERATOR'S INSTALLED MSI AT f02703e. Windows package, desktop shell and CI all pass. The MSI installs, the native window opens, the bundled node starts, and the handshake completes -- liberty-sidecar-ready {"host":"127.0.0.1","port":62699}, followed by "catalog metadata source: none requested", which proves instrumentation ran to completion and the sidecar process is healthy. The window then displays:

  Project Liberty could not start this page
  Something failed before the application frame could render.

THAT TEXT IS apps/web/src/app/global-error.tsx, AND IT IS THE ONE SCREEN IN THIS APPLICATION THAT CANNOT SAY WHAT WENT WRONG. The component's signature was `{ reset }` -- it never declared Next's `error` argument, so the error was dropped at the parameter list. It logged nothing. It showed no digest. And its own comment said "The log has it", which was FALSE: nothing anywhere wrote it. Three rounds of Windows work were spent guessing at a failure that was reporting itself to nobody.

WHAT ITS PRESENCE ALREADY TELLS US, AND IT NARROWS THE PROBLEM A LOT. global-error renders only when the render fails at or above the root layout. For the operator to be looking at it, the window had ALREADY navigated to the sidecar origin, the document request had ALREADY passed the 403 request guard, and Next had ALREADY served HTML. So this is not PL-0753's class and not the shell's supervision path -- surface_failure drives the bundled splash, which contains none of this text. It is a render or hydration failure inside the application.

WHAT THIS TASK DOES NOT DO, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST SHAPE OF IT: it does not fix the render failure. The failure cannot be identified from this session. The packaged production artifact was booted here and GET / answers 200 with the real application -- the app shell, the skip link, the navigation including Browse, 2 inline scripts and 10 script tags all carrying a CSP nonce. So the defect does not reproduce on Linux from the same tree, and nothing records it on Windows. This task makes it RECORD ITSELF, which is the only thing that can end the guessing.

REQUIRED: THE BOUNDARY RECEIVES THE ERROR AND SURFACES THE DIGEST. The existing reasoning was half right -- a root-layout failure can carry a stack trace and a digest is the only thing safe to show. It then omitted the digest too. A digest is Next's own correlation id, lowercase hex, no message and no path; showing it is what lets an operator quote one line that matches a line in the log. When Next minted none, the page says so rather than leaving a blank where a reference should be.

REQUIRED: THE REPORT REACHES THE FILE THE OPERATOR ALREADY PASTES. The Rust shell captures the sidecar's stdout and stderr, redacts tokens, budget-caps the volume and writes %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.projectliberty.desktop\logs\sidecar.log. A browser-side failure had no route into it -- console.error in the page goes to the webview's console, which nothing captures. One POST to a local diagnostics route closes the gap and adds no file, no port and no new place to look.

REQUIRED: NO MESSAGE AND NO STACK CROSS THAT BOUNDARY. A message from a server component can carry a file path, a connection string, a query or a token; a stack carries build paths. The report is five bounded fields -- boundary, pathname with the query and fragment REMOVED, digest matched against lowercase hex, error name matched against an identifier pattern, and hadMessage as a BOOLEAN so a reader can tell an error that said nothing from one whose text was withheld. The server re-sanitises with the same rules rather than believing a body because it came from our own page.

REQUIRED: THE REPORTER CANNOT BE THE FAILURE. It is called from the last-resort boundary, which must not import the shell, the stylesheet, or anything that could be what just failed. The module imports NOTHING -- no React, no CSS, no contract package -- is total against anything JavaScript can throw including a throwing getter, and swallows every failure of its own.

REQUIRED: A REFUSAL LEAVES A TRACE. The request guard answers 403 with no body and no reason, deliberately, so the wire cannot be used as an oracle for which check failed -- and the consequence nobody accounted for is that a refusal left no trace ANYWHERE, which is why "does the installed WebView get 200 or 403" was unanswerable from the machine that served it. The wire is unchanged. The server-side log records the method, the path without its query, and whether a token header and a Host header were PRESENT -- no header value, and not which check failed. Between them those separate a webview that never attaches the token from one that attaches it to some requests and not others, from a Host mismatch, from a request that is not ours.

REQUIRED: BOTH LOGS ARE BUDGETED. One refused page load is dozens of refusals and a remount loop reports continuously; the line that matters is the first one. The budget keeps the first few per window, drops the rest, and says once per window how many it dropped -- so the log states that it stopped recording rather than appearing to say the failures stopped.

MUST NOT: weaken the request guard, change what the wire says, widen what the 403 reveals, or record any header value, token, query string or user data.

MUST NOT: claim the startup failure is fixed. It is not diagnosed. What this earns is that the next MSI run will say what failed, in the file the operator already sends.

review.title: There is no way to browse the catalog: home shows two rails and search needs you to know the answer
review.acceptance:
THE GAP. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md names "Home/catalog/search" among the MVP capabilities. Home and search exist; there is no catalog surface. Browsing is currently two home rails -- RAIL_DEFINITIONS in lib/catalog.ts, films and series, newest first -- plus a search box that requires the viewer to already know what they are looking for. A viewer who wants to see what is in the catalog, or everything in one genre, has nowhere to go. /browse, /catalog, components/browse and any live-TV route do not exist in apps/web/src/app.

REQUIRED: A BROWSE SURFACE THAT READS THE SAME PORT THROUGH THE SAME GATES. The catalog metadata port (lib/catalog-source-registry.ts), then selectDeclaredItems, then isSurfaceable, then the browsable-kind allowlist -- the order home and search both already apply, and in that order, so a record whose rights basis the source did not declare is never reachable from this surface either. No new provider, no new fixture, no second catalog read path.

REQUIRED: THE FACETS ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT SURVIVED THE RIGHTS GATE, NOT FROM THE RECORDS. A genre list is published to the reader. Deriving it before the gate would let a withheld record contribute a genre name -- disclosing that the catalog holds something of that kind while refusing to show it, which is a rights leak through a filter control rather than through a card. The facet list must be computed from the surfaced items only, and a test must pin that ORDERING. The test needs a cast to do it, and the cast is itself the finding: contentRightsSchema admits only the three playable values, so every schema-valid CatalogItem is surfaceable and the union cannot express a withheld one -- the real withholding happens upstream in selectDeclaredItems, which refuses a record before it becomes an item at all. The ordering is still load-bearing against the rights vocabulary being widened later, which is the only way it can regress, and the test says so rather than implying the type system proves it.

REQUIRED: 'YOUR FILTERS MATCHED NOTHING' AND 'THE CATALOG HAS NOTHING' ARE DIFFERENT PAGES. This is the collapse app/search/search.ts documents at length and lib/catalog.ts carries a cause field for. An empty browse result must say which of the two it is, and the cause must come from the catalog rather than be inferred from the length of a filtered array, because both states legitimately produce an empty array.

REQUIRED: DETERMINISTIC ORDER WITH A FINAL TIEBREAK, AND NO localeCompare. Same catalog and same filters in, same list out, on any host. localeCompare without an explicit locale uses the host's collation, which is the defect already removed from candidate ranking in @liberty/media-engine and from search's result sort; buildHomeCatalog still has it and is not this task's surface. id decides last, so the sort can never fall back on the order the catalog arrived in.

REQUIRED: THE FILTERS LIVE IN THE URL AND WORK WITHOUT JAVASCRIPT. A GET form and search params, so a filtered view is shareable and bookmarkable and so the surface is complete before hydration. Parameters arrive as untrusted input and are read defensively: a repeated parameter takes its first value rather than being joined, an unrecognised value falls back to the unfiltered default, and nothing malformed produces a 500 -- the rules readSearchQueryParam already states for q.

REQUIRED: THE NAVIGATION ENTRY, AND A GUARD THAT THE PROMISE IN THAT FILE IS KEPT. navigation.ts's header says "every entry goes somewhere that exists" and nothing checks it: the existing test only asserts that a live href starts with a slash. A live entry whose route file is absent is exactly the dead link that file was written to remove, so the guard must resolve each live href to a page under apps/web/src/app and fail when one is missing.

MUST NOT: add a play affordance to a browse card, imply a resolvable stream from an item being visible, or weaken any rights gate. Browse is discovery; a stream is resolved through authorized provider adapters at playback time.

MUST NOT: add an HTTP contract or a route handler. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md requires schemas in @liberty/contracts before a route exists, and it lists no browse route among the planned contracts. This value is computed in the server render and nothing transports it, so a wire contract would be contract machinery with no transport. GET /api/v1/search is the planned route that would change that, and it is not this task.

MUST NOT: claim e2e coverage that was not run. The Playwright suite cannot be executed in this session; the surface is covered by vitest, the route is reachable through the navigation guard, and the e2e spec is deliberately left to a task that can run it rather than shipped unexecuted into a 45-minute job.

review.title: The player has no rate, no subtitle styling, no sync offset and no resume rule -- and no way to test one if it had
review.acceptance:
THE SHAPE OF THIS TASK, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST ONE. apps/web/vitest.config.ts is environment: "node": there is no DOM, no HTMLMediaElement and no app-router context, so no control can be verified by driving a real element here. Every item below is therefore delivered as a pure model over a narrow injected port plus an adapter, and the classification of what is actually proven is part of the deliverable.

REQUIRED: PLAYBACK RATE AS A CLOSED SET, NOT A NUMBER. An arbitrary rate is a way to hand the element a value it will clamp silently. The allowed rates are enumerated, a requested rate is resolved to the nearest allowed one, stepping saturates rather than wrapping, and the adapter refuses an off-list rate rather than clamping it a second time. The element is the authority on the current rate: the adapter publishes what the element reports and publishes nothing for an unreadable reading rather than emitting NaN.

REQUIRED: SUBTITLE STYLING THAT CANNOT CARRY CSS. A stored style is attacker-influenced data the moment it round-trips through a profile record. Styling is therefore tokens only, decode reports a named reason per rejected field, and a stored value such as a colour with a trailing declaration is REFUSED rather than sanitised -- sanitising is the weaker property, because it claims to have removed everything dangerous.

REQUIRED: OFFSETS THAT DO NOT DRIFT. Subtitle and audio synchronisation offsets snap to integer steps so repeated nudges cannot accumulate float error, saturate at their bounds, and have a reset.

REQUIRED: A RESUME RULE WITH AN ABSTENTION. Near the start and near the end both mean restart, not resume, and an unreadable position means the decision declines to supply one rather than supplying zero -- a resume decision that returns 0 is indistinguishable from "start at the beginning" and would silently discard a real position. Thresholds duplicated from the server module must be held to parity by a test that fails if either side moves.

REQUIRED: CAPABILITY DETECTION THAT NEVER CLAIMS HARDWARE. The probe reports what the browser reported and names its source; "unknown" is a first-class answer. A method read off a capabilities object must be invoked on its owner, or it throws.

REQUIRED: A DECLARATIVE KEYMAP. A key event resolves to a named command in a tested module and the component dispatches; no key reaches a seek fraction of 100%; a focused text input keeps its keys.

MUST NOT: promote an experimental native player, or presume the unresolved native-hosting decision. MUST NOT ship a control that moves and changes nothing -- a slider with no actuation is worse than its absence, because it reports a capability the product does not have. State plainly which items are models with no UI.

review.title: Live TV is a nav entry with no destination, and no code that could read a playlist if a licensed feed arrived
review.acceptance:
THE BOUNDARY THIS TASK IS WRITTEN AROUND. Live acquisition is blocked on licensed feed access and stays blocked. What is missing is not a channel source: it is the parsing, authorization, organisation and presentation layer that a licensed feed would feed, and the tests that would catch it being wrong. Building that layer must not create a path by which a synthetic fixture reaches a viewer looking like a channel.

REQUIRED: BOTH PARSERS ARE HAND-WRITTEN AND TOTAL. No parsing dependency is added. The M3U reader returns per-line diagnostics instead of throwing, and handles the real malformations: quoted attributes with escaped quotes, a BOM, CRLF, a missing trailing newline, an entry with no URL, an attribute with no value, duplicates. It never follows a URL. The XMLTV reader REFUSES a DOCTYPE or entity declaration outright rather than attempting to parse it safely -- that is the XXE class, and refusal is the only property worth asserting -- and is bounded in input size.

REQUIRED: TIME ZONES ARE DATA, NOT AN ASSUMPTION. A timestamp's offset is parsed from the feed, instants are stored in UTC, and rendering takes the zone from the caller. Offsets that are not whole hours, a programme crossing midnight and a programme crossing a DST boundary are each tested.

REQUIRED: NOW AND NEXT COME FROM AN INJECTED CLOCK. Logic that reads Date.now() internally cannot be tested at a boundary, and the gap case -- nothing scheduled -- must be a named state rather than an empty object.

REQUIRED: THE RIGHTS GATE IS ON THE PATH, NOT BESIDE IT. Every channel reaches the surface through the existing authorization, each rejection carries a named reason, and a channel whose origin is not held is dropped rather than shown with a warning.

REQUIRED: THE SHIPPED CONFIGURATION TELLS THE TRUTH. With no licensed feed registered, /live states that no feed is configured. A test must scan the surface's own modules and FAIL if any of them names the fixtures directory, a fixture filename, or calls the feed registrar -- because the tempting move, with a finished parser and no feed, is exactly to register the fixtures so the screen has something on it.

REQUIRED: ERROR REPORTING THAT LEAKS NOTHING. A stream failure is reported as a named class, with no URL and no credential in the message.

MUST NOT: bundle a channel list, hard-code a third-party credential, make a network call, or weaken the gate. Fixtures must be obviously synthetic so that no reader can mistake one for a shipped channel.

review.title: Watchlist, history, resume and preferences are four unrelated reads, so switching profile switches some of them
review.acceptance:
THE DEFECT. Per-viewer state was reached through several independent reads with no single notion of whose state it is, so there was no one place that could answer "is this snapshot the active profile's" and no one place a reset could act on. A failed read answered with an empty list, which is indistinguishable from a profile that genuinely has nothing -- an absence standing in for a presence, again.

REQUIRED: ONE SNAPSHOT, ONE PORT, AND A FAILED READ THAT SAYS SO. Watchlist, favourites, Continue Watching, history and resume positions are one coherent per-profile model behind a narrow persistence port. A failed read answers null, never an empty collection, and staleness against the active profile is a value the caller can read rather than a thing it must infer. No port method takes a profile id: scope is derived server-side, so a caller cannot ask for someone else's state.

REQUIRED: PREFERENCES ARE VERSIONED AND THE MIGRATION IS TOTAL. A stored record written by an older build must never crash a newer one. The migration accepts anything, including a record of the wrong shape, and the test asserts that over hostile input rather than over the happy path.

REQUIRED: DELETION IS VERIFIED BY RE-READ, NOT BY STATUS CODE. A 204 proves a request was accepted, not that data is gone. Each reset that is implemented re-reads and asserts absence; each reset that is NOT implemented refuses honestly and names what it cannot remove. A control that appears to delete and does not is worse than no control.

REQUIRED: NO BROWSER STORAGE, STILL. This application deliberately uses no localStorage and no sessionStorage, and two existing tests enforce it. Persistence goes through the server-side repository.

REQUIRED: THE TWO UNGUARDED MODERN APIs ON THIS SURFACE ARE GUARDED. Intl.Segmenter is constructed and destructured in the avatar path and Object.hasOwn is read in the watchlist path; both run inside the application shell on the installed WebView2 build that is currently failing with a client TypeError. Guard the property access itself, the construction, and the destructuring -- the iterator is a separate failure point from the constructor -- and make the fallback correct for astral characters rather than returning a lone surrogate.

MUST NOT: introduce an account system, a cloud dependency or a sync service. MUST NOT fabricate a favourites feature: if there is no store for it, report not-implemented.

[chromium] tests/critical-journey.spec.ts:876 the player page offers a way back same pair THE DEFECT IS NOT THE STRING. Wave 132 (PL-0760) made the home hero LOADER-DRIVEN so the first screen can state a fact about this installation instead of a fixed sentence. These two tests pinned that sentence, and the comment above the first one stated the reason it was safe to pin: "the hero is static markup rendered by the page itself, ABOVE the boundary the catalog load sits inside". That premise is now false. Correcting the assertion and leaving the sentence would have left a comment that lies about why the test exists, which is worse than the failure. REQUIRED: THE INVARIANT ASSERTED MUST BE ONE EVERY BRANCH CAN SATISFY. The hero has four branches -- a spotlight title, an empty cause, a recognised error reason, an unrecognised one -- and no string is common to them. What is common is 200 and EXACTLY ONE h1: a page with none gives a screen reader nothing to land on, a page with two has no single title. It must be held from the other side as well, by a unit test that drives every branch, or the e2e assertion is satisfiable by a page with the wrong heading. REQUIRED: THE THIRD ASSERTION, WHICH DID NOT FAIL AND IS STILL WRONG. The refused branch of "which catalog the home route can serve" matches /couldn.t load the catalog/i. `catalogErrorCopy` now maps `catalog_source_not_configured` to "No catalog source is configured"; "We couldn't load the catalog" survives only as the fallback for a reason this build does not recognise. That branch is skipped in the development configuration, and the production and fail-closed configurations could not start their web server because the build was broken -- so it did not fail, and it would have failed on the next green build. Fixing it in the same change as the two that did fail is the point: a round that fixes only what the log printed leaves the next failure for the next round. MUST NOT: pin another build-dependent string, weaken an assertion to a status code or a `toHaveCount(0)` that an empty page would satisfy, or delete a test. Each correction must be shown to be necessary -- the old assertion must be demonstrated to fail against the current build, not assumed to.

THE GAP, AND IT IS WHY FOUR CONSECUTIVE ROUNDS SHIPPED A BROKEN INSTALLER WITH GREEN CHECKS.

packaged-server-smoke.mjs boots the packaged sidecar and fetches `/`. Since Wave 131A it also requires the application frame's markers and refuses the error headline. All of that is necessary and NONE of it executes JavaScript. The Wave 132 failure is a TypeError thrown while a client module is being EVALUATED -- the report's frames resolve to the Turbopack ESM instantiation chain -- and a fetch of server-rendered HTML cannot observe that at any cost. The HTML was always correct. The application never started.

REQUIRED: THE PACKAGED ARTIFACT IS RUN IN A REAL BROWSER. Relocated outside the repository, booted with a real sidecar token, and driven with a real engine that evaluates the client bundle. Nothing less can see a module-evaluation failure.

REQUIRED: THREE INDEPENDENT CHANNELS, EACH ABLE TO FAIL ALONE, because the recurring defect class here is a check whose shape an absence satisfies.
  (1) THE DOM: the frame's markers present AND no boundary headline present. Either half alone is satisfiable by a failure -- markers-only passes a page that rendered then threw, headline-only passes a blank page.
  (2) pageerror: an uncaught exception reaching the window, which a module-evaluation throw produces BEFORE any boundary exists to catch it.
  (3) THE DIAGNOSTICS ROUTE: a POST to /api/v1/diagnostics/client-failure means a boundary fired and reported, in the same vocabulary the operator's log will carry.
A pass requires all three clean. The self-test below demonstrates that they are genuinely independent rather than three spellings of one check.

REQUIRED: A SELF-TEST THAT INVERTS THE SCRIPT. It injects a module-evaluation TypeError and requires the script to FAIL. A qualification test nobody has shown can fail is a green light with no lamp in it, and this project has already shipped three of those.

REQUIRED: THE SCRIPT STATES WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, in its output and not only in a comment. It runs Chromium. The installed application runs WebView2 inside the Tauri shell, and the Wave 132 failure reproduces there and not under Chromium -- so a pass means "the packaged bundle starts under Chromium", never "the MSI starts". Claiming otherwise would be the fabrication the operating contract forbids by name.

REQUIRED: AN ABSENT BROWSER IS A SKIP WITH EXIT 2, NOT A PASS. e2e/ is deliberately outside the workspaces so a browser download is not a prerequisite of npm ci; a qualification script that silently passes when it could not launch anything is worse than one that is not run.

MUST NOT: be wired into a workflow file in the declaring round -- .github/workflows/ci.yml, windows.yml and desktop-shell-ci.yml are all reserved by tasks in REVIEW. The script must therefore be runnable by one documented command, and the fact that nothing schedules it yet must be reported rather than implied away.
review.notes: FILED 2026-10-13 after the operator's installed MSI at faa6e8a failed to start while CI, Windows package and the packaged smoke were all green.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The script was written and committed before the task was filed, because the task's acceptance is derived from what the operator's crash report proved about the gap -- that nothing executes the client bundle -- and that was only established by resolving the three turbopack frames. faa6e8a is the commit the installed MSI was built from and the last commit before any of this script exists.

integration.evidence:
INTEGRATION at b14848c4978f96d8ae700158fdc95a885f09f1f5. EXECUTED AGAINST THE PACKAGED ARTIFACT IN A REAL BROWSER, both ways.

NORMAL RUN -- node apps/desktop/scripts/packaged-startup-qualification.mjs, 8 checks, all passed:
  ok  the packaged tree was relocated outside the repository
  ok  the relocated sidecar starts and announces a port (bound 43217)
  ok  the packaged homepage answers 200 (16461 bytes)
  ok  the application frame rendered (carries skip-link, class="shell", id="main")
  ok  no error boundary is on screen (neither "could not start this page" nor "Something went wrong")
  ok  the home page rendered exactly one h1
  ok  no uncaught exception reached the window (pageerror never fired)
  ok  no client failure was reported (no POST to /api/v1/diagnostics/client-failure)

SELF-TEST -- the same script with --self-test, which injects a module-evaluation TypeError and requires the script to FAIL. It failed, as required:
  FAIL  no uncaught exception reached the window
        TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'selfTest')
  SELF-TEST PASSED: the injected module-evaluation TypeError was detected.

AND THE SELF-TEST TAUGHT SOMETHING THE DESIGN ONLY ASSERTED. Of the three channels, ONLY pageerror caught the injected failure. The DOM channel stayed clean (the application still rendered, because the injected throw was not in the app's own graph) and the diagnostics channel stayed clean (no boundary fired). That is the empirical proof that the three channels are independent rather than three spellings of one check -- and it means a single-channel version of this script, which is what a first draft would have been, would have passed the injected failure.

WHAT EACH CHECK WOULD STILL BE SATISFIED BY, stated because that question is what this project's last four regressions turned on:
  - "answers 200" alone: an error page, a 404 body, an empty body. Which is why it is never alone.
  - "frame rendered" alone: a page that rendered the shell and then threw during hydration.
  - "no boundary headline" alone: a blank page, a 404, a network failure.
  - "exactly one h1" alone: an error boundary, which also renders exactly one h1. Deliberately so -- that is why it sits beside the headline check rather than replacing it.
  - pageerror alone: a failure React caught and reported without ever reaching the window.
  - the diagnostics POST alone: a failure that threw before any boundary existed to report it -- which is precisely the Wave 132 case.
No single check is load-bearing. All three channels must be clean.

A MISSING BROWSER IS A SKIP WITH EXIT 2 AND SAYS SO IN WORDS ("THIS IS A SKIP, NOT A PASS: nothing was qualified"), because e2e/ is deliberately outside the workspaces and a browser is not guaranteed present. A script that silently passes when it could not launch anything is the failure mode this task exists to remove, in a new place.

ENVIRONMENT, stated because it bounds the claim: run under Chromium build 1194 via LIBERTY_QUALIFICATION_CHROMIUM, resolving Playwright from e2e/node_modules. The script prints, on every run, that it does NOT prove WebView2 compatibility.

NOT SCHEDULED BY ANYTHING YET. .github/workflows/ci.yml and windows.yml are reserved by PL-0736 and desktop-shell-ci.yml by PL-0746, both in REVIEW, so wiring this into a job would collide with a reserved surface. The one place that currently executes scripts on windows-latest is package-sidecar.mjs, which is PL-0755's surface and has been reopened four times already. So this round delivers the script and one documented command, and the fact that nothing runs it automatically is a known limitation rather than an omission.

recommended.title: The distribution inventory runs nowhere until the Windows workflow calls it
recommended.acceptance:
REQUIRED: the Windows package job runs scripts/windows/distribution-inventory.mjs against the PACKAGE BUILD OUTPUT after the bundle is produced, and against the INSTALLED TREE inside the lifecycle run, with each invocation naming which tree it is reporting on. Two trees, two reports, never conflated.

REQUIRED: it runs even when a later step fails, for the same reason the installer-log upload does -- the inventory of a build is most interesting on the run that went wrong.

REQUIRED: its unit suite joins npm run test:scripts, and therefore gains a step in the CI validate job, because PL-0714's mirror-check fails a build whose alias names a suite with no step. A script nothing runs is this repository's most-repeated defect and PL-0737 must not become the sixth instance.

OUT OF SCOPE: what the inventory says. This task makes it run and makes its output readable.
recommended.notes:

SURFACE CORRECTED 2026-10-05, BEFORE THE NEXT CLAIM RATHER THAN DURING IT. The task could not satisfy its own third clause. That clause requires the inventory's unit suite to join `npm run test:scripts` and therefore to gain a step in the CI validate job -- because PL-0714's mirror-check fails a build whose alias names a suite with no step -- and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was not among allowedPaths. Whoever claimed it would have reached that clause, found the file outside the surface, and either widened it mid-implementation or quietly skipped the clause. Both are worse than fixing the declaration while nobody owns the task.

ADDING ci.yml MEANS THIS TASK NOW OVERLAPS PL-0736 UNTIL THAT ONE CLEARS REVIEW, and that is the correct state rather than an obstacle: `ai:claim` will refuse, which is the control plane saying the two cannot safely be held at once. It was already refusing on windows.yml alone.

recommended.title: test:scripts and the CI validate job can disagree in one direction without anything noticing
recommended.acceptance:
FILED ON A FALSE PREMISE AND REWRITTEN BEFORE ANY WORK. The original said apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs "is run by nothing" and called it the fifth instance of a suite no gate asks. IT RUNS IN CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml, validate job, step id `notices-suite`, `node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs`, added by PL-0714. The claim came from reading that file's own header comment -- "NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY RUNS THIS FILE AUTOMATICALLY YET" -- which was true when PW-0208 wrote it and was made false by PL-0714 a round later. The correction is recorded as a defect.found event.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND IT IS SMALLER AND MORE INTERESTING.

1. THE SUITE IS NOT IN `npm run test:scripts`, so it is not in `npm run check` either. It runs on every push and never on a developer's machine through the command this repository tells people to run. That is a coverage asymmetry, not an absence.

2. PL-0714's `mirror-check` CANNOT DETECT THAT, and this is the finding worth the task. It derives the alias's scripts from package.json, derives the job's from the workflow, and fails when a script in the ALIAS has no STEP. The reverse -- a step with no alias entry -- is not checked in either direction. Measured: adding notices.test.mjs to the alias makes the check report "every suite in the alias has a step in this job" and exit 0, and removing it again also exits 0. The mechanism PL-0714 built to end a hand-kept list is itself one-directional, so half the drift it was built for is still invisible.

REQUIRED: `npm run test:scripts` names the suite, so `npm run check` covers it locally.
REQUIRED: the mirror check becomes BIDIRECTIONAL -- a suite step in the validate job with no entry in the alias fails too, with the same kind of message. PL-0714's own words apply: "the note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step did not keep it in step on any of the three occasions", and a one-directional check is half a note.
REQUIRED: both directions are proven to FAIL, by removing an entry from each side in turn and showing the check goes red, not merely by showing it green today.
REQUIRED: the stale header comment in notices.test.mjs is corrected, because it is what produced the false premise above. A comment that outlives the code it describes is the failure this project keeps recording.

OUT OF SCOPE: making apps/desktop an npm workspace. Round 106 measured that and it breaks repo:validate; the account is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.
recommended.notes:
FILED ROUND 111 by claude-infra during PW-0208, ON A FALSE PREMISE, and rewritten the same round by claude-lead after checking the workflow rather than trusting a comment. Surface widened from package.json alone to include ci.yml (the mirror check lives there) and notices.test.mjs (its header carries the stale claim). Priority dropped P2 -> P3: a local-coverage gap and a one-directional check, not a suite running nowhere.

COLLIDES WITH: .github/workflows/ci.yml is PL-0717's (REVIEW) and PL-0726's (REVIEW) surface, so this cannot be active beside either. That is why it is not being executed now.
